name: FileBot
description: FileBot is the ultimate tool for organizing and renaming your movies, tv shows or anime, and music well as downloading subtitles and artwork. It's smart and just works. The graphical user interface (GUI) of the application can be accessed through a modern web browser, requiring no installation or configuration on the client side, or via any VNC client. The container is built against Alpine Linux to provide an efficient image in terms of size and resource usage. For a complete documentation of this container, see https://github.com/jlesage/docker-filebot#readme

paths.name: Config Directory
paths.description: Stores the application's configuration, state, logs, and any files requiring persistency.

paths.name: Storage
paths.description: Contains files from the host that need to be accessible to the application.

paths.name: Automated Media Center: Watch Directory
paths.description: This is the input folder of the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. Any media copied to this folder will be processed by the script.

paths.name: Automated Media Center: Output Directory
paths.description: This is the output folder of the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. This is where medias are located once they are renamed and organized.

ports.name: WEB Port for GUI (Bridge Network Type)
ports.description: Port to access the application's GUI via the web interface. NOTE: This setting is relevant only when the Network Type is set to `Bridge`.

ports.name: VNC Port for GUI (Bridge Network Type)
ports.description: Port to access the application's GUI via VNC protocol. Optional if no VNC client is used. NOTE: This setting is relevant only when the Network Type is set to `Bridge`.

variables.name: User ID
variables.description: ID of the user the application runs as.

variables.name: Group ID
variables.description: ID of the group the application runs as.

variables.name: Umask
variables.description: Mask controlling permissions for newly created files and folders, specified in octal notation.

variables.name: Niceness (priority)
variables.description: Priority at which the application should run. A niceness value of `-20` is the highest, `19` is the lowest and `0` the default. NOTE: Setting a negative value requires additional permissions. Thus, `--cap-add=SYS_NICE` must be added to Extra Parameters (shown when Advanced View is enabled).

variables.name: Display Width
variables.description: Width (in pixels) of the application's window.

variables.name: Display Height
variables.description: Height (in pixels) of the application's window.

variables.name: Dark Mode
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables dark mode for the application.

variables.name: Web Audio
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables audio support, allowing audio produced by the application to play through the browser.

variables.name: Web File Manager
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables the web file manager, allowing interaction with files inside the container through a web browser, supporting operations like renaming, deleting, uploading, and downloading.

variables.name: Web File Manager Allowed Paths
variables.description: Comma-separated list of paths within the container that the file manager can access. By default, the container's entire filesystem is not accessible, and this variable specifies allowed paths. If set to `AUTO`, commonly used folders and those mapped to the container are automatically allowed. The value `ALL` allows access to all paths (no restrictions).

variables.name: Web File Manager Denied Paths
variables.description: Comma-separated list of paths within the container that the file manager cannot access. A denied path takes precedence over an allowed path.

variables.name: Web Desktop Notifications
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables the web notification service, allowing the browser to display desktop notifications from the application.

variables.name: Web Terminal
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables access to a terminal from the web interface. It is strongly recommended to configure the container with secure web access (HTTPS).

variables.name: Web Terminal
variables.description: The shell used by the web terminal.

variables.name: Web Authentication
variables.description: When set to `1`, protects the application's GUI with a login page when accessed via a web browser. Access is granted only with valid credentials.

variables.name: Web Authentication Token Validity Time
variables.description: Lifetime of a token, in hours. A token is assigned to the user after successful login. As long as the token is valid, the user can access the application's GUI without logging in again. Once the token expires, the login page is displayed again.

variables.name: Web Authentication Username
variables.description: Optional username for web authentication. Provides a quick and easy way to configure credentials for a single user. For more secure configuration or multiple users, see the documentation.

variables.name: Web Authentication Password
variables.description: Optional password for web authentication. Provides a quick and easy way to configure credentials for a single user. For more secure configuration or multiple users, see the documentation.

variables.name: Secure Connection
variables.description: When set to `1`, uses an encrypted connection to access the application's GUI (via web browser or VNC client).

variables.name: Secure Connection VNC Method
variables.description: Method used for encrypted VNC connection. Possible values are `SSL` or `TLS`.

variables.name: Secure Connection Certificate Check Interval
variables.description: Interval, in seconds, at which the system checks if web or VNC certificates have changed. When a change is detected, affected services are automatically restarted. A value of `0` disables the check.

variables.name: Web Listening Port (Non-Bridge Network Type)
variables.description: Port used by the web server to serve the application's GUI. This port is internal to the container and typically does not need to be changed. NOTE: This setting is relevant only when the Network Type is set to something else than Bridge.

variables.name: VNC Listening Port (Non-Bridge Network Type)
variables.description: Port used by the VNC server to serve the application's GUI. This port is internal to the container and typically does not need to be changed. NOTE: This setting is relevant only when the Network Type is set to something else than Bridge.

variables.name: FileBot GUI State
variables.description: Setting this to `1` enables the FileBot GUI, `0` disables it.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: State
variables.description: Setting this to `1` enables the Automated Media Center (AMC) script, `0` disables it.

variables.name: OpenSubtitles Username
variables.description: Username of your OpenSubtitles (https://www.opensubtitles.com) account. Required to download subtitles.

variables.name: OpenSubtitles Password
variables.description: Password of your OpenSubtitles (https://www.opensubtitles.com) account. Required to download subtitles.

variables.name: Custom Options
variables.description: Custom arguments to pass to FileBot. This applies to the UI only.

variables.name: Use FileBot Beta Version
variables.description: When set to `1`, FileBot installed under `/config/beta` (container path) is used. If no FileBot installation is found under this folder, the latest beta version is automatically downloaded during container startup. See (#using-a-beta-version) section for more details. **NOTE**: Use at your own risk. Beta version may have bugs and stability issues.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Interval
variables.description: Time (in seconds) between each invocation of the Automated Media Center (AMC) script.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Input Stable Time
variables.description: Time (in seconds) during which properties (e.g. size, time, etc) of files in the watch folder need to remain the same before invoking the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. This is to avoid processing the watch folder while files are being copied.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Action
variables.description: Action performed by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script on files. Valid values are `test`, `copy`, `move`, `symlink`, `hardlink`, `keeplink`, `duplicate` or `clone`. Use the `test` operation to perform a dry-run and verify that everything gets matched up correctly.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Conflict Resolution
variables.description: Conflict resolution strategy used by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. When set to `skip`, existing files are never overriden, while `auto` overrides existing file only if new media is better.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Match Mode
variables.description: Match mode used by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. The `opportunistic` mode works for all files regardless how badly they are named, while `strict` mode works for reasonably well-named files and ignore files that cannot be matched accurately. See https://www.filebot.net/forums/viewtopic.php?t=4695 for complete documentation.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Artwork
variables.description: When set to `y`, artwork is fetched and NFO file is generated by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Language
variables.description: Language used by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script to rename files. Two-characters language code or value like English, French, German, Chinese, etc can be used.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Music Format
variables.description: Define how music files are renamed by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. Filebot supports a very powerful naming scheme. See https://www.filebot.net/naming.html for complete documentation.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Movie Format
variables.description: Define how movie files are renamed by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. Filebot supports a very powerful naming scheme. See https://www.filebot.net/naming.html for complete documentation.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: TV Series Format
variables.description: Define how TV series files are renamed by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. Filebot supports a very powerful naming scheme. See https://www.filebot.net/naming.html for complete documentation.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Anime Format
variables.description: Define how anime files are renamed by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. Filebot supports a very powerful naming scheme. See https://www.filebot.net/naming.html for complete documentation.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Process Music
variables.description: When set to `y`, music files are processed by the Automated Media Center (AMC) script. A value of `n` does not process them.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Subtitle Languages
variables.description: Comma-separated list of subtitle languages to download. Example: `en,de,fr`.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Custom Options
variables.description: Custom arguments to pass to the Automated Media Center (AMC) script.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Input Directory
variables.description: Directory inside the container used as the input folder of the Automated Media Center (AMC) script.

variables.name: Automated Media Center: Output Directory
variables.description: Directory inside the container used as the output folder of the Automated Media Center (AMC) script.
